text:
The scoreboard said a rout, but the chances said something much closer. Anaheim won 5-1 in Winnipeg, yet the Ducks deserved to win only 53 percent of the time across simulated replays of every shot, and the Jets outattempted them 53 to 39. Both teams put 17 shots on goal. The gap was finishing and goaltending. Lukas Dostal faced 2.34 expected goals and allowed one, saving about 1.34 more than an average goalie would have. Clay Stevenson allowed four on 2.48 expected, about 1.52 goals worse than average.

For two periods it stayed tight. Judd Caulfield opened the scoring in the first with a snap shot at 14:41, and Tim Washe made it 2-0 at 5:20 of the second on a snap shot that carried only a 19 percent chance. Winnipeg actually had the better of the second period by expected goals, 0.84 to 0.81, but trailed by two anyway.

The third period is where the game was won. Anaheim generated 2.09 expected goals to Winnipeg's 0.94 and scored four times. Sam Colangelo made it 3-0 early in the period, Kyle Connor answered at 10:36, and Mikael Granlund restored the three-goal lead on a 2 percent chance. Nikita Nesterenko closed it at 19:19 on an 83 percent chance. Caulfield, Washe and Jeff Malott took the three stars, with Beckett Sennecke driving much of the play, as Anaheim was out-chanced for the night but won the stretch that counted.
